raw_response.publication_year_note: Published 1 August 2014 in BMC Research Notes 2014, 7:486 (Received: 18 July 2014; Accepted: 24 July 2014; © 2014).
raw_response.rationale: This process evaluation of India's Total Sanitation Campaign (TSC) across 100 cluster-randomised villages in Orissa reports three distinct sets of quantitative findings: (1) descriptive-only latrine coverage contrasts for overall intervention progress (8% at baseline to 66% in March 2012, p. 4) and Below Poverty Line vs Above Poverty Line cardholders (68% vs 61%, p. 4, after implementers exercised discretion to extend subsidies to all households to avoid conflict, p. 7), with no SEs, CIs, or p-values; (2) inferential village-level t-tests between intervention and control arms (Table 2, pp. 8-9, n = 807 households) that test campaign/VWSC awareness rather than sanitation access (failing Criterion 4); and (3) inferential village-level linear regressions across the N = 50 intervention villages (Table 4, p. 11; built from n = 408 households and n = 170 Village Water and Sanitation Committee [VWSC] members) testing associations between village-level latrine coverage in March 2012 (Criterion 4 sanitation coverage) and mandated TSC governance, participatory targeting, and outreach/support mechanisms. Specifically, active functioning of the TSC-mandated VWSC (>=5 VWSC meetings held since programme start: beta = 0.178, 95% CI 0.010 to 0.346, p = 0.04) and household outreach visits by village motivators (beta = 0.216, 95% CI -0.000 to 0.431, p = 0.05 in Table 4; p = 0.02 on p. 7) show positive associations with village latrine coverage, alongside non-significant estimates for participatory wealth ranking (used to identify poor non-BPL households for subsidy eligibility; beta = 1.530, p = 0.42), PRA mapping/transect walks (beta = 0.637, p = 0.09), and NGO training of VWSC members (beta = 0.001, p = 0.99). These Table 4 estimates fit SWiM Family B (assistance/participation/external-support, with secondary governance overlap with Family A/C for VWSC institutional activity). Confidence is rated medium because under an ultra-strict reading of narrow Criterion 2 requiring formal legal/rule-status variation rather than variation in de facto VWSC meeting regularity, participatory targeting, and outreach intensity across villages under uniform TSC rules, Table 4 sits near the implementation-fidelity boundary while the strict BPL-card rule contrast (68% vs 61%) is descriptive only.
